new_statements.quote: 4. — En Ido, la acento tonika ne esas plualtigo o plulongigo dil sono, ma plufortigo di la voco sur un silabo dil vorti. On pozas lu « sur la lasta silabo dil infinitivi e sur la prelasta silabo di la cetera vorti » : amâr, venîr, skribôr; fenêstro, bovîno, malâda, trôno, mêa, puêri, opiniôno, e. c. « Ma en plursilaba radiki, i e u nemediate avan vokalo ne darfas recevar l'acento » : Kâspia, râdie, fîlii, mistêrio; tênua; êlua, sêxuo, stâtui, lînguo (1). Pro ke la finali ia, ie, ii, io, e ua, ue, ui, uo di ca lasta vorti formacas nur un silabo, la prelasta esas reale ta, qua preiras li, ed ol portas la acento tote konforme al regulo.
new_statements.translation: 4. In Ido the tonic accent is not a raising or lengthening of the sound but a strengthening of the voice on one syllable of the word. It is placed 'on the last syllable of infinitives and on the penultimate syllable of all other words': amâr, venîr, skribôr; fenêstro, bovîno, malâda, trôno, mêa, puêri, opiniôno, etc. 'But in polysyllabic roots, i and u immediately before a vowel may not receive the accent': Kâspia, râdie, fîlii, mistêrio; tênua; êlua, sêxuo, stâtui, lînguo. Because the endings ia, ie, ii, io and ua, ue, ui, uo of these words form only one syllable, the penult is really the one preceding them, and it bears the accent fully in accordance with the rule.
new_statements.citation: Beaufront, Louis de. 1925. Kompleta Gramatiko Detaloza di la Linguo Internaciona Ido. Esch-Alzette (Luxemburgia): Meier-Heucke.
new_statements.locator: Sec. 4 'Acento tonika', p. 11 of the archive.org transcription (pdf p. 11); footnote (1) p. 12 quoting Akademio decido 57, Progreso III, 322

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress (intensity) falls on the penultimate syllable of every polysyllabic word, except that verb infinitives (-ar, -ir, -or) are stressed on the final syllable. For the count, an i or u immediately before a vowel in a polysyllabic root does not form its own stressable syllable (lînguo, mistêrio), so stress lands on the preceding vowel; monosyllabic roots in -i/-u keep the stress (dîo, glûo, also in compounds arborglûo); weekday names sûndio etc. stress the syllable before -dio; au/eu penults stress the a/e.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Explicitly discouraged: after stressing the penult one must not add a quasi-second accent on the grammatical ending ('evitez sentigar quaze duesma acento sur la dezinenco: Esperântô, harmôniô').
new_statements.exceptions: Infinitives -ar/-ir/-or final-stressed (by analogy with Romance -ar); iV/uV in polysyllabic roots unstressable; monosyllables may be stressed or not by context; numerals 20-90 keep stress on the unit root (dúadek); dek-e-un stresses dek; foreign proper names (Profilaktol, Kashmir, Portugal) keep their own accentuation; elision of final -a does not move the stress (sec. on eliziono).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level prescriptive rule of a planned language (Akademio decision 57, c. 1910); applies to full inflected word forms including desinences; the 1907 original grammar had plain penult stress on all words with no infinitive exception.
new_statements.identity_note: Ido (idoo1234, ISO ido), the reformed-Esperanto planned language; the 1925 KGD describes standard Ido as fixed by the Akademio after decision 57. The 1907/1908 Grammaire complète describes the earliest stage (uniform penult stress, no infinitive exception) and is superseded.

sources.note: Sec. 4 'Acento tonika' (pp. 11-13): stress (intensity, not pitch/length) on the last syllable of infinitives (-ar, -ir, -or) and on the penult of all other words; in polysyllabic roots i/u immediately before a vowel cannot bear stress (Kâspia, lînguo), but monosyllabic roots keep it (dîo, glûo, arborglûo); au/eu diphthong penults keep stress on a/e; monosyllables free; no secondary stress on the desinence. Quotes Akademio decido 57 (Progreso III, 322). Appendix 1 (pp. 148ff.) gives the history of the decision.

sources.note: Preliminary lesson on pronunciation, printed p. 1 (pdf p. 15): 'The Accent or stress of voice falls (1) on the last syllable of the infinitive (-ar, -ir, -or); (2) on the last syllable but one of other words. (3) But in polysyllabic roots, i and u immediately before a vowel cannot receive the stress.' Same rule in English.
